about.title: San Fernando Wrongful Death Claims
about.longDescription: Losing someone in a preventable collision changes everything, and San Fernando families often find themselves navigating grief alongside unfamiliar legal questions. Local roads like San Fernando Road, N Maclay Avenue, and Truman Street see steady traffic, and crash reports show collisions cluster on Thursday afternoons between 5 and 7 p.m., a reminder that ordinary commutes can turn tragic. California law allows certain surviving family members, starting with a spouse, domestic partner, or children, to pursue a wrongful death claim against the party responsible. These cases are separate from any criminal charges that may follow a fatal crash. LawProactive is not a law firm; we're a free service that connects grieving families in San Fernando with an independent attorney who can review what happened, explain who qualifies to file, and pursue compensation for funeral costs, lost financial support, and the loss of a loved one's guidance and companionship. You focus on your family, we handle the introduction.

whyChoose.title: What San Fernando Families Should Know

items.title: Only Certain Family Members Can File
items.desc: California limits standing in a wrongful death case, usually to a spouse, domestic partner, or children first, with other dependents or heirs eligible in some situations. An attorney can help determine who in your family qualifies to bring the claim.

items.title: The Clock Starts Ticking Quickly
items.desc: You generally have two years from the date of death to file a wrongful death claim in California, though claims against a government entity require much faster action. Waiting too long can permanently close the door on recovery.

items.title: Recoverable Losses Go Beyond Bills
items.desc: California law allows families to seek funeral and burial expenses, lost financial support the deceased would have provided, and compensation for the loss of love, companionship, and guidance. An independent attorney can help identify every loss that applies to your family's situation.

items.question: How long do we have to file a wrongful death claim in San Fernando?
items.answer: Generally, California law gives surviving family members two years from the date of death to file. If the responsible party is a government agency, such as the city or county, the deadline is much shorter and requires an early formal claim. Speaking with an attorney soon after a loss helps preserve your options.

items.question: Which roads in San Fernando see the most crash activity?
items.answer: Public collision records point to Truman Street, San Fernando Road, Glenoaks Boulevard, and N Maclay Avenue as higher-volume corridors, with reported crashes tending to peak on Thursdays between 5 and 7 p.m. These are simply patterns in the data, not a judgment about any specific location. An attorney can review the details of your family's incident regardless of where it occurred.

items.question: Can our family recover money if criminal charges are also filed?
items.answer: Yes, a wrongful death claim is a separate civil action from any criminal case tied to the same crash. Even if criminal proceedings are ongoing or have concluded, your family can still pursue compensation through a civil claim. An independent attorney can explain how the two processes typically move on different timelines.
